It rained hard yesterday morning.
I took my umbrella and got on the bus to go to work.
The bus was crowded, and I had to stand near the door.
I found a seat after a few stops.
I put my umbrella under the seat and looked at my phone.
The ride was long, about thirty minutes, and I almost fell asleep.
Music played softly from someone's earphones nearby.
The bus stopped near my office, and I got up fast.
I grabbed my bag and walked off the bus.
I didn't think about my umbrella at all.
My mind was already on the busy morning ahead of me.
I walked into my office building, and the rain was still falling outside.
I reached into my bag for my umbrella, but it wasn't there.
I checked every pocket, but I couldn't find it.
Then I remembered.
I had left it under the bus seat.
I felt annoyed, but there was nothing I could do.
The bus was already gone, and it wasn't coming back for my umbrella.
I worked all day, and the rain didn't stop.
By the evening, I needed to go home, but I had no umbrella.
I stood at the bus stop and watched the rain.
Water ran down the street in small rivers.
A woman next to me had a big umbrella.
She saw me standing there without one, and she smiled.
She asked if I wanted to share her umbrella to the train station.
I said yes, and we walked together under her big umbrella.
We didn't know each other, but we talked the whole way.
She told me she also lost an umbrella last week, on a train.
We laughed about it.
Losing umbrellas seemed to happen to everyone.
At the station, I thanked her, and she said it was no problem at all.
She said she hoped I found a new one soon.
The next day, I bought a new umbrella.
It was blue, with small white dots on it.
This time, I wrote my name on it with a marker.
I also made a rule for myself: check my seat before I leave.
I still think about that first umbrella sometimes.
Maybe someone found it on the bus.
Maybe they are using it right now, on a rainy day like this one.
Now, every time I ride the bus, I check under my seat before I stand up.
It only takes two seconds, but it saves me a lot of trouble.
My umbrella problem taught me a small but useful lesson.
I don't want to lose another one.
